title: Kagoshima / Ryukyu 1879: three Army Ministry cipher drafts in the 1877 kana substitution tables (nos. 4, 1, 6), contemporary plaintext on the drafts

steps.what: JACAR item pages and PDFs fetched; the JACAR 内容 field interleaves the cipher and the plaintext columns, which is why the record strings look partly in clear.
Headers 四号 / 第六号 and the cipher-plaintext pairs identified as tables 4, 1 and 6 of the 1877 Army tables (C09084568800); all 22 tables are shifts (8 - 2n mod 44) of one sequence.

Frozen protocol: each documentary table applied to the plaintext reproduces the transcribed cipher for 95/96 (doc 1), 45/47 (doc 2) and 132/138 (doc 3) signs; 200 controls (the 21 other tables + 179 random alphabets) reach at most 0.188, 0.255, 0.174. The pre-registered H1 (one key learned on doc 1, applied to doc 2) failed (0.021), as the drafts use different tables.
Contemporary kana plaintext segmented, put into kanji and translated; doc 2 sign テ/マ settled by the cipher (レ = マ in table 1).

Contributor's pre-registered hypothesis H1: one key learned on doc 1 and applied to doc 2. 0.021 of signs agree; the drafts use different tables. Declared failed; the per-document-table addendum came after this result (by the contributor's record).

Integration check: a decoder written for the check from the reversed-iroha sequence reproduces 95/96, 45/47, 132/138 signs with tables 4, 1, 6; other shifts at most 0.021, 179 random alphabets at most 0.170. JACAR PDFs fetched; 52 cipher signs on frames 0533 and 0575 compared with the transcription, 52 agree.
Tomokiyo's Cryptiana page opened: it describes the 1877 22-table system (reversed iroha, shift of two per table), so the key structure is published; no reading of these drafts there.

Siblings: the neighbouring JACAR records C10072242100 and C10072244300 are the Ministry's kanji drafts of docs 1 and 3; doc 3's open stretch is 食料ヲ除キ準備ノ目途ヲ以テ and doc 1's 御考ヘ is confirmed; 98/99 words, sure only.

outcome.method_basis: The clerk wrote the plaintext kana beside the cipher on each draft; it is transcribed and put into kanji, and the cipher is checked against tables 4, 1 and 6 of the Army's 1877 kana tables (C09084568800); the Ministry's kanji drafts of docs 1 and 3 settle the words the kana left open.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Integration check, 13 Nov 2026, sure words only (probable words are holes): doc 1 35/35, doc 2 19/20, doc 3 44/44 (contributor's word units) = 98/99 = 99.0%. The contributor's figure was 96/99 = 97.0% (sure and probable words, doc 3 41/44), made before the Ministry's kanji drafts of docs 1 and 3 (JACAR C10072242100, C10072244300) were found.

credits.note: plaintext kana written beside the cipher on the three Army Ministry drafts (1879), and the Ministry's kanji drafts of docs 1 and 3 (C10072242100, C10072244300)
describes the Army's 1877 kana tables 第一号-第二十二号 (reversed iroha, each table shifted two places) on Cryptiana; the key applied here is that system
PR #536: transcription of the three drafts, identification of tables 4, 1 and 6, kanji, translation and check of the cipher against the tables

texts.label: Army Ministry draft, 1879: Kagoshima dispatch, notes (catalogue 2572)
texts.summary: The Kagoshima garrison's dispatch is not a campaign, so no campaign allowance; departure date not fixed; spare ammunition better sent from here.

reading_review.note: contemporary plaintext, 35/35 words; 御考ヘ confirmed by the kanji draft C10072242100; checked against table no. 4 (95/96 signs)

texts.label: Army Ministry draft, 1879: no huts to be built for the troops sent to Ryukyu (catalogue 2573)
texts.summary: No need to build huts for the troops sent to Ryukyu; Captain Masumitsu informed as well.

reading_review.note: contemporary plaintext, 19/20 words sure; the name マスミツ (益満?) not identified; checked against table no. 1 (45/47 signs)

texts.label: Army Ministry draft, 1879: half battalion of Kagoshima ordered to Ryukyu (not in the catalogue)
texts.summary: Half the Kagoshima garrison ordered to the Ryukyu domain (1 March 1879); the other half, which may be ordered out at any time, is to prepare under articles 2 and 4-7, food excepted, and report missing items.

reading_review.note: contemporary plaintext, 44/44 words; the open stretch settled by the Ministry's kanji draft C10072244300 (食料ヲ除キ準備ノ目途ヲ以テ); checked against table no. 6 (132/138 signs)

gaps.item: doc 2, the name マスミツ (益満?)
gaps.detail: kana certain from cipher and plaintext; the kanji and the officer need an 1879 Army officer list, not reached online

gaps.item: doc 1, short struck-out passage after トウチヨリ
gaps.detail: struck through in both columns on the draft and not part of the message; not counted

prior.where: The contemporary plaintext is written beside the cipher on each draft (JACAR images). The 1877 tables are in JACAR C09084568800; the 1876-77 table system is described by Satoshi Tomokiyo, Cryptiana, meijiarmy.htm. No reading of these three drafts found in print or online (JACAR, Cryptiana, this repository, web search JA, 13 Nov 2026).

human: Brice Dudout chose the targets and set the rules (protocol frozen by SHA-256 before any key test); a Claude agent fetched the JACAR images, transcribed, identified the tables, ran the frozen check and wrote up. No human visual review yet.
